tagline: Across the Mississippi on a bridge that opened before its scheduled debut
intro: The Zachary Taylor Parkway connects small towns and agricultural country across Louisiana and into Mississippi. Its Mississippi River crossing carries four lanes on the John James Audubon Bridge, with two-lane roads linking the crossing to LA 1 and US 61.

The bridge changed the parkway’s river crossing in 2011, replacing the ferry between New Roads and St. Francisville. Its opening had been expected in June, but rising water closed the ferry and brought the bridge into service on May 5.

Begin at the Alexandria and Pineville end of the corridor. At the Mississippi, cross from the New Roads side toward St. Francisville; LA 10 then passes through Jackson toward Clinton. Bogalusa stands at the junction of LA 10 and LA 21, in pine-forest country where the Great Southern Lumber Company developed a mill town in the early twentieth century.

moments.title: Forts Randolph and Buhlow
moments.text: At Pineville, the Forts Randolph and Buhlow State Historic Site includes the remains of Bailey’s Dam. The dam allowed Admiral David Porter’s Union fleet to pass below the Red River rapids during the retreat after the Battle of Mansfield. The historic site combines the two forts with a visitor center and elevated boardwalk.

moments.title: John James Audubon Bridge
moments.text: The Mississippi River brought forward this bridge’s opening. Rising water had stopped the New Roads–St. Francisville ferry, so the new crossing opened on May 5, 2011, ahead of the expected June debut. It carries LA 10 and the Zachary Taylor Parkway between Pointe Coupee and West Feliciana parishes. The cable-stayed span between its towers measures 1,583 feet. Sliding joints accommodate movement between the decks, with a travel allowance of 49 inches. It is the only bridge over the Mississippi between Natchez and Baton Rouge, replacing the ferry link between New Roads and St. Francisville.

moments.title: Clinton
moments.text: Clinton became a parish seat because Feliciana Parish was divided. Residents in the west had complained that bad weather made travel to the government offices in Jackson difficult. In 1824, the legislature split the parish, choosing Clinton for East Feliciana and St. Francisville for West Feliciana. Clinton remains East Feliciana’s parish seat.
